newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast approves Shell oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast approves Shell oil deal.

text.p: Ivory Coast has approved its first hydrocarbons deal for a deep water offshore block and it hopes the involvement of oil major Shell will attract investment from other big firms, a government statement said on Thursday.
Shell and UMIC, a subsidiary of Houston-based United Meridian Corp, were expected to sign the production-sharing deal for block CI-105 next week.

"Shell International is the world's biggest oil company and its involvement in the Ivorian offshore sector illustrates well its intention to embark upon some very ambitious investments in our country," the statement said.
"It is certain that this will have a decisive impact on the interest of other major international oil firms with regard to our deep offshore areas," it said.
UMIC is the main partner in a group exploiting oil and gas reserves in nearshore block CI-11. It currently produces about 20,000 barrels per day of oil and 60 million cubic feet of gas a day.
Ivory Coast adopted a new hydrocarbons code last July which gave special incentives like longer permit validity to help defray the high cost of deep water exploration.
Mines and Energy Minister Lamine Fadika is due to tour Europe and North America from the middle of this month with the aim of promoting Ivory Coast's hydrocarbon and mineral reserves.
The CI-105 deal was approved at a cabinet meeting on Wednesday.
